root_cause.statement: contact.organizationId - the persisted default org that login pins the active context to - is NEVER validated against BlockingStatuses, while contact.organizations correctly filters blocked orgs out of the eligible list. So login pins the user to an org the same backend just excluded, and every org-scoped query then returns Forbidden inside an HTTP 200.
root_cause.retracted_hypothesis: An earlier synthesis blamed the storefront for omitting organization_id from the token grant. That is wrong as a root cause: the org-SWITCH grant does carry organization_id (verified on the wire: grant_type=refresh_token&organization_id=organization-acme-store). The login password grant does omit it, but the defect is the unvalidated server-side default, not the client.
root_cause.fix_location: server-side - validate contact.organizationId against BlockingStatuses when resolving the login active-org context (vc-module-customer OrganizationIdClaimProvider / OrganizationIdRequestValidator area)
root_cause.frontend_contribution: renders the active org as a [selected] switcher option even when it is absent from the eligible list - which is incidentally what gives multi-org users their escape hatch

c40_refinement.finding: For a user with legacy org associations but NO OrganizationMembership row, effective status resolves entirely from contact.Status, so a blocking global status denies EVERY org - and the C-41 membership-override remedy is unavailable because no row exists to override with. Verified live on MULTI_ORG_USER (11 orgs, 0 rows): Invited -> user_invitation_pending_in_organization, Rejected -> user_is_rejected_in_organization, restored to Approved -> 200.
c40_refinement.population: 104 of the 105 at-risk accounts on this env have no membership row
c40_refinement.healthy_baseline: With contact.Status=Approved and no membership row, myStatusInOrganization resolves to Approved and an org-scoped token is issued with full permissions - the fallback works correctly
